lead: >-
  The adventures on a journey combining Argentina, Colombia and Peru begin at Iguazu Falls, continue along Peru's high-altitude roads to Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu, and end with a trip to the El Peñón de Guatapé rock in Colombia. These are stages of a much larger eight-country tour, not a standalone adventure trek across three countries. Compare the physical demands and travel times between stops.

## What the adventure portion of the itinerary includes

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. One suitable option is the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The selected countries appear at different stages of the itinerary: Argentina comes closer to the beginning, Peru follows Bolivia, and Colombia is the final destination. The tour also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Chile and Ecuador.

Adventure is a secondary interest on this itinerary. It includes mountain roads, visits to natural landmarks, excursions and long journeys between destinations, but **there is no confirmed Inca Trail hike or independent mountain ascent in each of the three countries**. Choose the trip based on its actual day-by-day itinerary and the physical preparation required.

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls

In [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travelers visit the Argentine side of the falls in a group with a Russian-speaking guide. The excursion is followed by a flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where the program includes a city tour and a tango show with dinner.

The natural highlights of this stage are the humid forest, cascading waterfalls and viewpoints along the falls. Walking here is different from a multi-day trek. Comfortable shoes and protection against spray are useful, and it is worth discussing a suitable pace and which park trails are accessible in advance. The [group tour of Iguazu Falls](/argentina/puerto-iguazu/iguazu-argentina-group-russian-program/) is confirmed, but more demanding activities should not be added to the list of included services without evidence.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca, the high Andes and Machu Picchu

The Peruvian stage begins after Bolivia. Following the border crossing near Desaguadero, travelers stop at [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and visit the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The next day features a [tourist-bus journey from Puno to Cusco](/peru/puno-and-lake-titicaca/puno-cusco-andes-tourist-bus/) with stops at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani, La Raya Pass and Pucará.

Altitude is a key consideration on this stretch. Long journeys through the Andes, changing temperatures and frequent stops require stamina even when much of the day is spent in a car or bus. [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and the Titicaca region sit well above sea level, so it makes sense to consider acclimatization and any personal health restrictions before traveling.

A separate day is dedicated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The confirmed program includes a group excursion with an English-speaking guide, lunch and a train journey back to Cusco. **There is no multi-day Inca Trail hike to Machu Picchu**. Travelers explore an archaeological site in a mountain setting, but the experience is different from a sporting trek.

Afterward, the itinerary includes the [archaeological sites around Cusco](/peru/cusco/cusco-archaeological-sites-russian-guide/) and a sightseeing tour of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). In Peru, adventurous scenery is combined with Inca history, guided road excursions and cities.

## Colombia: the Guatapé rock and contrasting landscapes

The Colombian stage starts with a flight to Medellín. A dedicated excursion takes visitors to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) with an English-speaking guide. The eight-hour outing covers several locations and views of the reservoir among the hills.

The itinerary confirms a visit to the rock, but **does not specify whether climbing the steps to the summit is included**. The possibility, duration and conditions of the climb should be agreed separately. Travelers then visit [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), Cartagena, Bogotá and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/): these are mainly city and cultural excursions.

| Country | Activities on this stage |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Walks around Iguazu Falls |
| Peru | Andean roads, Titicaca, Machu Picchu |
| Colombia | Guatapé and the surrounding hills |

## How to assess the itinerary before booking

The central practical question is not the number of countries but the combination of high altitude and long transfers. Titicaca and Cusco have cool highland conditions, Iguazu has a humid natural environment, and Cartagena lies on the tropical Caribbean coast. Layers of clothing, sun protection and sturdy footwear for natural and archaeological sites are useful on this route.

Altitude affects people differently and is not necessarily linked to athletic fitness. Before traveling through the Andes, it is sensible to discuss medical restrictions with a doctor and consider the earlier high-altitude days in Bolivia. When choosing the intensity of excursions, allow enough recovery time after long journeys and flights.

Ada Tours helps match the desired level of activity to the actual excursions, plan the sequence of transportation and identify stages where a gentler pace may be possible. Travel documents and entry requirements must be checked against the traveler's nationality and all eight countries on the full route, not just the three named in this catalog.

## Compare your options

The [general Argentina + Colombia + Peru catalog](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru/) lists programs regardless of interest, while [multi-country adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) offer other active travel options to compare. If archaeology and historic cities are more important, the same three countries also have a [culture and history selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru/interests/culture-and-history/).

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions

### Is an Inca Trail hike included?

No. The program includes an excursion to Machu Picchu, after which travelers return to Cusco by train.

### Is mountaineering experience required?

This is not advertised as a mountaineering tour. However, the high-altitude stages in Peru and Bolivia require individual consideration of health and altitude tolerance.

### Can I climb El Peñón de Guatapé?

A visit to the rock is included. Whether the climb to the summit is part of the excursion and whether it is available on the chosen date must be confirmed separately.

### Why is an eight-country tour listed under three countries?

Because these three main countries form a selection within a much longer itinerary. The actual tour is not limited to Argentina, Colombia and Peru.

## Three countries, three different cultural experiences

[Argentina](/argentina/) introduces travelers to Buenos Aires' neighborhoods and tango traditions. [Peru](/peru/) offers a journey from Andean cultures to Inca-era monuments and colonial architecture. [Colombia](/colombia/) continues the trip through cities with very different histories: Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. This sequence makes the combination appealing to travelers who choose a journey for its culture and history.

One option is the [“Eight South American countries in 32 days” tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). In addition to these three countries, it visits Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. It is **not a separate 32-day tour exclusively through Argentina, Colombia and Peru**. The [general selection for these three countries](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru/) groups together longer routes that include all three among their main destinations.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Argentina: historic neighborhoods and live tango

After visiting the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls, the group arrives in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The itinerary includes a city tour with a Russian-speaking guide, followed by a tango show with dinner in the evening. Together, these experiences introduce the city: first its streets, architecture and historic districts, then music and dance as part of the capital's cultural life.

The sightseeing day covers [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), La Boca, Recoleta and Puerto Madero. Travelers especially interested in tango history should clarify the evening's format beforehand: the published itinerary confirms **a show with dinner**, not a private dance lesson or a visit to a music archive. Those experiences would need to be arranged separately.

## Peru: from Andean heritage to Lima

Travelers enter Peru from Bolivia, near Lake Titicaca. The journey from [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is itself a cultural route, with stops at Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Pucará and La Raya Pass. It is followed by an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and visits in Cusco to Qorikancha, Sacsayhuamán and other architectural and archaeological sites.

After Cusco comes [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), including Miraflores, the main square, the cathedral or the MALI museum, depending on availability. This introduces another historical setting: the urban and religious architecture of the colonial period. If the main reason for the trip is an in-depth exploration of Inca monuments, it is more useful to allow additional time around Cusco than to squeeze several more cities into an already full day.

## Colombia: urban history, art and different eras

The Colombian section starts in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). Travelers visit El Peñón and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), explore Comuna 13, then fly to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Cartagena includes a sightseeing excursion through the historic city, taking in San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, old streets and squares. This provides an interesting contrast to Peru: instead of Inca structures, visitors encounter a port city shaped by Spain's colonial legacy.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the itinerary includes the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, the main square and Monserrate. The following day features a visit to Zipaquirá and its Salt Cathedral. The Colombian stage therefore offers several distinct cultural themes: Medellín's urban memory, Cartagena's fortifications, and the museums and religious landmarks of the capital region.

## Why the order of countries matters

On the published itinerary, Argentina comes before Peru, while Colombia follows Ecuador. Between Buenos Aires and the Inca heritage sites lie Uruguay, Chile and high-altitude Bolivia. Peru is followed by a flight to Quito, a trip to the Galápagos Islands and then Colombia. This sequence affects the trip's length, altitude exposure and number of flights. It cannot be presented as a short “Buenos Aires — Cusco — Bogotá” trip at the same price with the same services.

For a shorter cultural itinerary, we can discuss priorities: keep Buenos Aires and its tango evening, allow time for Cusco and Machu Picchu, and focus the Colombian section on Cartagena and Bogotá or on Medellín's modern history. Flights and guides would then need to be arranged afresh. Other existing options can be compared in [Colombia's cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/) and [multi-country culture and history itineraries](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural journey

### Is Cartagena included in the current itinerary?

Yes. The published 32-day tour includes a flight from Medellín to Cartagena and a tour of its historic center, including San Felipe de Barajas Fortress.

### Can I see Machu Picchu and Bogotá's museums on the same trip?

Yes. Both are included in the wider itinerary: first the excursions in Peru, then Ecuador and Colombia. A trip limited to those two cities would require separate arrangements for flights and a shorter program.

### Which is better for urban culture, Buenos Aires or Medellín?

Buenos Aires focuses on historic neighborhoods and an evening of tango. Medellín offers an introduction to the city and Comuna 13. Both stops complement each other for a wider cultural experience, but they are part of a 32-day journey through other countries as well.

## Iguazu, Titicaca and Guatapé: the natural geography of a grand tour

Traveling from [Argentina](/argentina/) to [Peru](/peru/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) means crossing a substantial part of South America. These countries do not share one single type of landscape: Argentine Iguazu is all about water and humid forest, the Peruvian Andes bring altitude, mountain passes and Lake Titicaca, while Colombia's Guatapé offers rock formations and an expanse of water surrounded by hills.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. You can choose the [“Eight South American countries in 32 days” tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It is important to understand the full geography from the outset: in addition to the three named countries, the itinerary covers Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. This tour is designed as a broad introduction to the continent, combining flights and city excursions with dedicated days in nature.

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls on both sides of the border

The journey to Argentina's [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) begins after a visit to the falls on the Brazilian side. An excursion through the Argentine section follows. This sequence offers two perspectives on one natural complex: surrounding forest, branching waterways, cascades and different viewpoints.

UNESCO lists Argentina's Iguazú National Park as a natural World Heritage Site and describes a vast waterfall complex within remnants of the Atlantic Forest. The experience is not only about the volume of falling water but also the humid forest ecosystem. Encounters with particular rare animals are not guaranteed as part of the excursion.

After Iguazu, the route continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). This tour does not travel to Patagonia or include the national parks of southern Argentina. It is worth noting because nature tours in Argentina are often associated with glaciers and mountains that are not included in this offer.

## Peru: the highlands of Titicaca, mountain passes and Machu Picchu

Peru follows the Bolivian stage. The itinerary includes travel to [Puno on Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The high-altitude lake and surrounding slopes are strikingly different from hot, humid Iguazu; days here combine natural scenery with local communities and traditions.

The next major stretch is a tourist-bus journey from Puno to Cusco, with stops along the way, including at high-altitude La Raya Pass. The road itself provides an introduction to the Andes' topography, but it is a bus trip with sightseeing stops, not an independent mountain trek.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is included as a full-day excursion from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Although best known for its Inca architecture, the site is surrounded by steep slopes and mountain ecosystems. Peru's national protected areas service, SERNANP, describes the historic sanctuary as containing a range of natural habitats at different elevations. The published excursion, however, focuses on the archaeological monument itself; no multi-day Inca Trail hike is specified.

## Colombia: El Peñón, Guatapé and Bogotá's elevation

The route through [Colombia](/colombia/) begins in Medellín and continues with an excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). This day includes [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and an introduction to the surrounding area. The enormous rock, water and hilly shores contrast sharply with Iguazu's scenery and the Peruvian highlands.

Cartagena and Bogotá follow. [Monserrate in Bogotá](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) rises above the city and offers views of the terrain on the eastern side of the Andes. It is part of a sightseeing program in the capital, however, not a separate extended ascent. This reflects the Colombian section overall: natural landscapes are part of the experience, but most days focus on cities and history.

If you are interested solely in long hikes and remote mountain areas, this extensive sightseeing tour may be less suitable than a specialized itinerary. A more precise description is **varied natural scenery between cultural stops**.

## Comparing the nature-focused days in the three countries

| Section | What is actually included |
|---|---|
| [Argentina](/argentina/) | The Argentine side of Iguazu after the Brazilian side |
| [Peru](/peru/) | Titicaca, Uros, an Andean road trip and Machu Picchu |
| [Colombia](/colombia/) | El Peñón and the Guatapé area, views from Monserrate |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The full itinerary also includes Bolivia's Uyuni Salt Flat and high-altitude lagoons, the desert landscapes of northern Chile and Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. These are a substantial part of the natural appeal of all 32 days, but they fall **outside the three selected countries**. They should not be presented as stops in Argentina, Peru or Colombia simply to make the filtered selection sound more attractive.

## Altitude, acclimatization and transportation

Iguazu lies in the humid subtropics, while Titicaca and Cusco are at high altitude. Bolivia also includes highland stages before the journey enters Peru. Because of changes in elevation and frequent travel, it is important to discuss tolerance for physical exertion, rest periods and the need for medical advice when relevant health conditions exist. Highland sightseeing trips should not be described as sea-level strolls.

For the falls, protection from spray is useful; for the highlands, bring warm layers, sun protection and comfortable footwear. The city days in Colombia and the trip to Guatapé call for different clothing and preparation. One weather forecast will not cover all eight countries.

The itinerary includes international and domestic flights. Entry rules, transit requirements and baggage allowances must be checked for the full list of countries, including those between the Argentine, Peruvian and Colombian stages. Argentina, Peru and Colombia have different national currencies; the acceptance of US dollars in cash and the operation of specific bank cards cannot be guaranteed everywhere. Ada Tours helps coordinate the practical details of the trip, the excursions and connections.

Explore the [full Argentina — Colombia — Peru selection](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru/) or [nature tours across several countries](/multi-country/interests/nature/) if you would like to compare this trip with other combinations.

## Frequently asked questions about traveling through these three countries

### Does the itinerary include both Iguazu and Machu Picchu?

Yes. They are included at different stages of the [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), separated by other countries and overland journeys.

### Is a multi-day trek to Machu Picchu included?

No. The program specifies a full-day excursion from Cusco, not an independent multi-day hike along the Inca Trail.

### What are the best scenic sights in Colombia?

On this particular trip, [Guatapé and El Peñón](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) stand out. The views around Bogotá are also included, but as part of a city sightseeing day.

### Why does a tour filtered for three countries last 32 days?

Because the filter selects destinations within a program spanning eight countries. To assess how long the trip really takes, consult the complete itinerary and flight dates rather than only the three selected countries.

## What nature and wildlife experiences does this itinerary combine?

Our selection covering Argentina, Colombia and Peru includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Among them is the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Its main geography goes beyond these three: it also includes Brazil, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador. Argentina comes near the beginning, Peru closer to the middle, and Colombia is the final country.

That distinction matters for the “Wildlife and Safaris” interest. In Argentina, the itinerary genuinely passes through Iguazú National Park. Peru features Lake Titicaca and the mountain landscapes of the Andes. The Colombian portion includes the Guatapé rock and reservoir. But **no specialized safari, dedicated birdwatching excursion or guaranteed viewing of rare animals is advertised in these three countries**. To compare trips without this thematic filter, browse [all itineraries including Argentina, Colombia and Peru](/multi-country/argentina_colombia_peru/).

## Argentina: Iguazu forest, waterfalls and realistic chances of seeing wildlife

The excursion to the Argentine side of the falls begins in the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area. The national park protects part of the humid Atlantic Forest, home to numerous birds, monkeys, tapirs and large predators. UNESCO recognizes the region's exceptional biodiversity. **The presence of a species in the park does not mean a tour group will encounter it**: the outing primarily focuses on the waterfalls and their viewing paths.

The previous day, travelers see the falls from the Brazilian side. A visit to the Bird Park and the Macuco Safari are offered separately there, but **they cost extra**, so they must not be counted among the basic wildlife experiences included in the tour. Despite its name, “Macuco Safari” does not by itself confirm a dedicated wildlife-viewing tour. The Argentine day ends with a flight to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/); the published program contains no additional forest days.

Walking paths and viewing platforms at Iguazu are affected by water levels. The Argentine park authorities reported temporary restrictions on access to the Devil's Throat in 2026. Check which routes are open before your visit: access to every part of the falls cannot be promised regardless of the weather.

If your priority is more time in Argentina's natural environments, compare the [nature-focused tours of Argentina](/interests/nature/tours/argentina/) by the actual number of days spent in parks.

## Peru: high-altitude nature without a scheduled safari

The group enters Peru from Bolivia via Desaguadero. The first stage is [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) with a visit to the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). Next comes a bus journey to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), a full day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and a trip to Lima.

Here, the natural setting is experienced through the high-altitude shores of the lake, mountains and changing elevations. The journey also introduces life around Titicaca and Inca heritage. **There is no dedicated excursion to search for wild animals in Peru on this itinerary**. Birds spotted by chance along the road should not be presented as an included ornithological tour.

Altitude is an important consideration. The Peruvian section follows high-altitude stages in Bolivia; for travelers who struggle with elevation, this affects wellbeing, pace and the need to consult a doctor. Tickets to Machu Picchu and permitted visitor circuits are regulated by Peru's Ministry of Culture, so the specific entry option must be checked when booking. Compare other natural destinations in the [Peru nature-tour catalog](/interests/nature/tours/peru/).

## Colombia: Guatapé's lakeside views instead of a jungle expedition

Following the flight from Ecuador, the Colombian section begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). It includes an eight-hour excursion to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/), [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and the nearby reservoirs. The combination of green slopes, rock formations and water makes for striking scenery. A visit to the rock is included, but the original description does not confirm that climbing to the summit is compulsory or included.

The following days are devoted to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/), museums, history and an excursion to Zipaquirá. The presence of the Caribbean Sea on the route **does not imply a separate marine expedition or whale-watching excursion**. There is no advertised nature excursion to a Colombian national park either.

This mix suits travelers who want scenic panoramas alongside city experiences. Those prioritizing rainforests or birdwatching should compare the available programs in the [Colombia wildlife selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/colombia/).

## Why the main wildlife stage lies outside these three countries

On the full tour, travelers visit the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador after Peru. The itinerary first includes [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and its highlands. It then features **one boat excursion chosen from two alternatives**: to [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach, or to [South Plaza Island](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión. The chosen option is confirmed at booking.

This is the strongest wildlife-focused stage of the entire itinerary: the Galápagos are known for endemic iguanas, seabirds, tortoises and sea lions. Still, nobody can guarantee sightings of every species. Protected areas have rules governing the presence of a guide, behavior on marked trails and how far visitors must stay from animals.

That is why the Argentina, Colombia and Peru filter should be read alongside the **full itinerary**, not as a promise of special wildlife activities in each selected country. If animals are your primary reason for traveling, it makes sense to discuss the length and exact option for the Ecuadorian island stage first.

## Seasons, clothing and logistics

| Section | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| Iguazu | Humidity and spray |
| Peruvian Andes | Altitude and cold nights |
| Colombia | Contrast between Bogotá and Cartagena |

The journey covers tropical lowlands, high mountains and cities with very different weather. After humid Iguazu come the high-altitude stops of Bolivia and Peru, then Ecuador and Colombia, with warm Cartagena and cooler Bogotá. Comfortable non-slip shoes, light rain protection, warm layers for altitude and sun protection are more useful than one universal set of “jungle gear.”

On such a long journey, entry and transit requirements for **all eight countries** must be checked according to the traveler's nationality, along with passport validity and international-flight rules. The three selected countries have different national currencies: the Argentine peso, Peruvian sol and Colombian peso. Acceptance of foreign bank cards, fees and exchange options depend on the bank and location, so payment with a single card cannot be promised throughout the trip.

We help coordinate the order of destinations, connections, flights, transfers and document preparation for the traveler's nationality. Consult the [published tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) for the included excursions and price instead of treating them as the cost of a separate three-country journey.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Argentina, Colombia and Peru

### Can we be guaranteed to see a jaguar at Iguazu?

No. Jaguars inhabit protected forests in the region, but a standard waterfall excursion is not a safari with guaranteed sightings.

### Will we see animals at Lake Titicaca?

The program includes the lake and the Uros Islands; no dedicated wildlife-viewing excursion is advertised. Chance encounters with birds cannot be counted as an included service.

### Is a nature reserve on the itinerary in Colombia?

The confirmed nature-focused stop is the Guatapé rock and reservoir area. This tour does not include a dedicated trip to search for wildlife in Colombia.

### Are the Galápagos Islands included?

Yes, but they are in Ecuador, which is **outside the selected three-country group**. One of two marine excursions is offered on the islands; the option is confirmed at booking.

### Which entry rules apply?

Those for the complete eight-country itinerary and any transit airports. Requirements depend on nationality and travel documents; visas, medical requirements and payment options should be checked against official sources for the travel dates.

## Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia: how the countries connect on the actual tour

The four countries offer remarkably different experiences. [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) make it possible to compare two capitals of the Río de la Plata region. In [Peru](/peru/), the central part of the itinerary revolves around [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). [Colombia](/colombia/) brings the journey to a close with Medellín, Cartagena and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/).

It is especially important to distinguish the four selected countries from **the complete geography of the product**. The published [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) starts in Brazil, continues to Argentina with a day trip to Uruguay, and then visits Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia in that order. Colombia does not follow Peru directly, and Uruguay is not a separate multi-day resort stay.

## Uruguay: a ferry day trip from Buenos Aires, not an overnight stay

On this itinerary, Montevideo is visited on **a full-day excursion from Buenos Aires**. The morning includes a transfer to the port, a ferry crossing, a guided tour of the Uruguayan capital with an English-speaking guide, free time and the return journey. The next day, travelers depart Buenos Aires for Chile.

This arrangement allows a visit to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) without changing hotels for a single night. Ferry travel does, however, involve departure schedules, check-in, port control and the formalities of an **international** border crossing. Treating it as a casual “trip across the river” would be misleading. Check the departure terminal, required boarding time and transfer arrangements after returning.

When comparing this with an independent [journey around Uruguay](/uruguay/tour/), keep its purpose in mind: a short city visit provides an introduction to the capital but does not automatically include Punta del Este, Colonia del Sacramento or the wine regions. Those would require a different itinerary and additional days.

## Argentina: Iguazu and the capital before Montevideo

Before Uruguay, the group visits the Argentine side of Iguazu Falls and then travels to Buenos Aires. The capital offers a sightseeing excursion and an evening tango show with dinner. The result is a progression from natural scenery to city neighborhoods and a one-day ferry trip to a neighboring country.

[Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) on this itinerary is connected with a visit to the Brazilian side of the falls. These are different national parks, separated by an international border. The Brazil–Argentina crossing is therefore already part of the journey before the Uruguay excursion adds another crossing. Any document checklist needs to account for all actual entries, not just the number of countries named by the filter.

If your priorities in Argentina include museums, food or a visit to Patagonia, compare [tours of Argentina](/argentina/tour/) rather than assuming those additional regions are already included in the eight-country program.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu after a long mountain stage

The route reaches Peru from Bolivia via Tiwanaku and Desaguadero. It then continues to Puno, the floating reed islands of Uros, a bus journey to Cusco, an excursion to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and a flight to Lima. This is a substantial sequence of visits, different modes of transport and nights spent in several cities.

When planning this section, consider the differences between Lake Titicaca, Cusco and coastal Lima. The highlands are generally cooler, and altitude tolerance can affect the pace of excursions. Archaeological sites also require advance consideration of admission arrangements and how much time a sightseeing day actually allows. Mentioning Machu Picchu does not mean any additional trail or itinerary can be added freely without prior agreement.

The journey through Bolivia before Peru forms a significant part of the overall program. Leaving Bolivia out of a filtered catalog title does not mean it can automatically be removed from the schedule or the price.

## Colombia: three cities with different climates and attractions

After Ecuador, travelers fly to Medellín. The Colombian itinerary continues to Guatapé and El Peñón, Comuna 13, then Cartagena and Bogotá with Monserrate and a visit to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá. Flights connect the cities.

Packing for Colombia requires different considerations from Uruguay: Cartagena is on the warm Caribbean coast, while Bogotá is a high-altitude capital. The intensity of this stage comes from both its excursions and a succession of flights within a relatively short period. If you prefer several days by the sea to a busy sightseeing program, discuss those priorities before booking.

A visit to Cartagena should not be mistaken for a promise of a separate beach holiday: the published program includes the city and a sightseeing excursion. For other types of trip, explore [tours of Colombia](/colombia/tour/).

## Border crossings, currencies and extra time

Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia each have their own currencies and banking limitations. Argentina and Uruguay use different pesos, Peru uses the sol, and Colombia uses the Colombian peso. Sharing the name “peso” does not make them a common currency or give them a shared exchange rate. Paying for the tour in USD should not be confused with a guarantee that US dollar cash or every bank card will be accepted locally.

For the full trip, documents must also be checked for Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador, as well as transit airports. Special attention is needed for the Montevideo ferry trip, the overland Bolivia–Peru border crossing and numerous international flights. Visa requirements depend on nationality, passport and the particular entry route. Ada Tours helps prepare a coherent checklist, coordinate tickets and ground transfers, and allow sufficient buffer time, but the countries themselves set final entry conditions.

## Frequently asked questions about itineraries through Uruguay, Peru and Colombia

### Is an overnight stay in Montevideo included?

No separate overnight stay in Montevideo is included in the described 32-day tour: it is a full-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires and back. If you prefer a more relaxed stay in Uruguay, the itinerary would need to be adjusted.

### Can Argentina and Uruguay be treated as one border-free tourist area?

No. Even on a relatively short ferry crossing, travelers cross an international border and must check the documents and formalities applicable to their nationality.

### What connects Peru and Colombia on this tour?

Ecuador. After Lima, travelers visit Quito and the Galápagos Islands, then fly from Guayaquil to Colombia. A direct Peru–Colombia leg is not part of the published sequence.

### Is one bank card and US dollars enough for the entire journey?

That cannot be guaranteed. The countries have different national currencies, payment rules and availability of banking services. A backup financial plan is needed for all countries actually visited.

### Can the day in Uruguay be replaced with an extra day in Peru?

It is possible to request a customized itinerary, but that must be agreed before tickets are purchased. It would change the ferry excursion, flight schedule and likely the cost of services.
